Product change: private projects become actually private.

Projects have a `visibility` of `private`, `org` or `public`, and explicit project membership is already stored, but today a `private` project is visible to the whole organization like any other. Enforce it.

A `private` project, and everything in it, is visible to an actor only if at least one of these holds: the actor's role is `admin` or `owner`; the actor is platform staff; the actor is the project's lead; the actor has been added to the project as a project member. `org` and `public` projects are unaffected.

- Looking up the project, one of its issues, its board, or an issue's comment thread throws `NotFoundError` (exported from `src/server/services/_support.ts`), not a permission error.
- Writes that target the project or anything in it (creating, updating, changing the status of, moving, assigning or archiving its issues; posting, editing or deleting comments on them; updating, archiving or restoring the project) also throw `NotFoundError` and change nothing.

Changes to project membership or to the lead take effect immediately.

tasks.prompt:
Product change: un-assignment becomes its own domain event.

Today clearing an issue's assignee publishes a generic `issue.updated` with `changedFields: ["assigneeId"]`, so nothing downstream can tell that someone lost an issue. Introduce a new domain event `issue.unassigned` with payload `EventEnvelope & { issueId: IssueId; projectId: ProjectId; previousAssigneeId: UserId }` and make it a first-class event everywhere domain events are produced and consumed.

Producers:
- Clearing the assignee of an issue that has one publishes exactly one `issue.unassigned` (actor = the caller, `previousAssigneeId` = the old assignee) instead of `issue.updated`. Clearing the assignee of an issue that has none publishes nothing. Reassigning from one person to another is unchanged (`issue.assigned` only).
- New rule: when a member is removed from the organization, every live (non-archived) issue assigned to them is unassigned, publishing one `issue.unassigned` per issue with the remover as the actor. Archived issues keep their assignee.

Consumers:
- Audit log: each `issue.unassigned` records one activity row with the new action `"issue.unassigned"`, subject kind `issue`, subject id = the issue id, the issue's project id, and the event's actor.
- Notifications: the previous assignee receives a notification of the new kind `"issue_unassigned"`, following the existing rule that an actor is never notified about their own action.
- Outgoing webhooks: `"issue.unassigned"` is a webhook event type endpoints can subscribe to. Each subscribed, enabled endpoint gets one delivery per event whose payload is the event payload serialised as JSON, as for the other issue events; endpoints that did not subscribe get nothing.

The new activity action, notification kind and webhook event type must be accepted everywhere the existing ones are declared and validated. Update the visible tests that encode the old behaviour.

tasks.prompt:
Product change: archiving a project freezes it.

A project can be archived without archiving its issues (`archiveIssues: false`), and today those issues stay fully editable. New rule: while a project is archived, its issues and everything attached to them are read-only.

Every write that would modify such an issue or its sub-resources must throw `AlreadyArchivedError` (from `src/lib/soft-delete.ts`), change nothing and publish no domain event. That covers editing issue fields, changing status (including board moves), assigning and un-assigning, archiving the issue, posting / editing / deleting comments on it, and adding / removing attachments on it. In addition, the overdue sweep must never announce an issue of an archived project as overdue.

Reads (the issue, its comment thread, its attachments, lists, the board) keep working. Restoring the project lifts the freeze completely, including for the overdue sweep. Creating issues in an archived project is already refused and stays so. Existing checks keep their precedence: an actor who lacks the permission still gets a permission error, and an archived issue or comment still reports itself.
